chunks.arabic_text: سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا، الدِّيلَمِيُّ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عليه السلام).

translations.en: Sulaymān ibn Zakariyya, al-Daylamī. He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him).
A liar, a ghālī (exaggerator in the Imams' virtues).

en.summary: Sulaymān ibn Zakariyya al-Daylamī is recorded as a narrator of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), yet he is critically evaluated in *Kitab al-Du'afa* as a *kadhhab* (liar) and *ghālī* (exaggerator). This dual characterization highlights the Shia methodology of distinguishing between the authenticity of a hadith's chain and the theological reliability of the narrator, particularly regarding those prone to exaggeration in the Imam's status.
en.seo_question: Who is Sulayman ibn Zakariyya al-Daylamī and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: An exaggerator (specifically in the virtues of the Imams)
key_terms.الدِّيلَمِيُّ: From Daylam (a region in northern Iran)
